tools.name: browser_tabs
tools.description:
List the tabs open in the user's Chrome.

Only each tab's id, title and site (origin) are returned, never the full URL.

Returns a JSON object with ``tabs``: id, title, origin, active, and
opened_by_probe — true for a tab browser_open_tab opened, which
browser_close_tab may close without asking the user.

tools.name: browser_activate
tools.description: Bring a tab to the front so it can be screenshotted. May ask the user.

tab_id.description: A tab id from browser_tabs.

tools.name: browser_snapshot
tools.description:
Read a page: its visible text and its interactive elements.

Each element has a ``ref`` that browser_click and browser_type take. Refs are
only valid until the page changes; take a new snapshot after navigating or
clicking. The user may be asked to approve this for the site.

tab_id.description: The tab to read; the active tab if omitted.

tools.name: browser_screenshot
tools.description:
Take a screenshot of a tab's visible area.

The only way to see what a page draws rather than writes — a game on a canvas,
a chart, anything inside a frame browser_snapshot cannot read. Scaled to at
most 1568 px on its long side and sent as JPEG. A point in this image, in its
own pixels, is what browser_mouse takes as x/y.

tab_id.description: The tab to capture; the active tab if omitted.

tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.description:
Open a URL in a tab. The user is asked to approve unless the site is trusted.

When the page links to where you are going, click that link instead
(browser_click): the user watches a pointer follow your clicks, and an address
typed in shows them nothing of how you got there. Navigate to reach the first
page, an address the user gave, or a place nothing on the page leads to.

tab_id.description: The tab to navigate; the active tab if omitted.

tools.name: browser_click
tools.description: Click an element from the latest browser_snapshot.

tab_id.description: The tab; the active tab if omitted.

tools.name: browser_type
tools.description: Type into an input from the latest browser_snapshot, replacing its value.

tab_id.description: The tab; the active tab if omitted.

tools.name: browser_open_tab
tools.description:
Open a URL in a new tab, leaving the user's other tabs as they are.

Prefer this to browser_navigate when the user's current tab should be kept,
and like it, only for a page nothing on the current one links to — otherwise
click the link, so the user can follow.
The user is asked to approve unless the site is trusted.

active.description: Bring the new tab to the front.

tools.name: browser_close_tab
tools.description:
Close a tab.

A tab opened with browser_open_tab closes straight away. Any other tab is
the user's and they are always asked first — even on a site they trust —
because closing it can lose unsaved work.

tab_id.description: The tab to close, from browser_tabs or browser_open_tab.

tools.name: browser_scroll
tools.description:
Scroll the page, or with ``ref`` the panel or list that element sits in.

browser_snapshot already reads the whole page; scroll to bring something into
a screenshot, or to make a page load what it only loads on scroll (feeds,
lazy images) — then take a new snapshot. The user may be asked to approve.

ref.description:
An element from the latest snapshot whose scrollable container to
scroll; the whole page if omitted.

tab_id.description: The tab; the active tab if omitted.

tools.name: browser_drag
tools.description:
Drag an element onto another, or by a pixel offset (sliders, sortable lists).

Drop onto an element by ``to_ref``, or by ``to_text`` for a drop zone with
nothing clickable in it (a "Drop files here" box, a board column's heading),
or move by ``dx``/``dy`` pixels.
Elements marked ``draggable`` in browser_snapshot are drag sources. The events
are simulated, which some sites ignore — check the result with a new snapshot.
The user may be asked to approve.

from_ref.description: The element to pick up, from the latest snapshot.

to_ref.description: The element to drop it on, from the latest snapshot.

to_text.description: Visible text of the drop zone, when it has no ref.

dx.description: Pixels to move right (negative: left), when there is no to_ref.

dy.description: Pixels to move down (negative: up), when there is no to_ref.

tab_id.description: The tab; the active tab if omitted.

tools.name: browser_mouse
tools.description:
One mouse action: press, move, release, click, double_click, wheel — or a
whole stroke with path.

For what browser_click and browser_drag cannot express: drawing, a drag with a
pause in it, hovering to open a menu, a double click, a scroll-wheel turn over
a map or a canvas.

**To draw, use action="path"**: one call per stroke. It presses at the first
of ``points``, moves through the rest in order and releases at the last, so a
line, a curve or a whole outline is a single call. Give 2 to 500 points; more
points make a smoother curve. Lift the pen between strokes by making each one
its own path call. Use press, move and release only for a gesture that needs a
pause or a look at the page part-way through; each of those is a separate
call, and a chat turn allows a limited number of rounds.

By default events are **simulated**, which some sites ignore. ``native=True``
sends real input through Chrome's debugger instead — sites cannot tell it from
a person — and Chrome shows a "debugging this browser" bar on the tab while it
is in use. Try simulated first; use native when a site does not respond. If
the user cancels that bar, native input on the tab is refused from then on.

Target a point with ``x``/``y`` in the pixels of the latest browser_screenshot,
or an element's centre with ``ref``. The user may be asked to approve once; the
rest of the gesture on that tab and site then runs for a minute (real input
needs its own approval, even mid-gesture).

action.description: press, move, release, click, double_click, wheel or path.

ref.description: An element from the latest snapshot, instead of x/y.

delta_x.description: For wheel: pixels to scroll right (negative: left).

delta_y.description: For wheel: pixels to scroll down (negative: up).

native.description: Send real input through the debugger instead of simulated events.

tab_id.description: The tab; the active tab if omitted.

points.description:
For path: the stroke as [[x, y], ...] in screenshot pixels, 2 to 500
points, every one on the visible page.

tools.name: browser_bookmarks
tools.description:
Read the user's bookmarks, or search them.

The user is asked every time: bookmarks hold full URLs and belong to no site,
so there is no trusting them in advance.

query.description: Words to find in a bookmark's title or URL; all bookmarks if omitted.

limit.description: How many to return, at most 500.

tools.name: browser_record
tools.description:
Film a tab as a video of a scenario: start right before the scenario, do it, and
stop right after, giving each recording a descriptive name ("checkout with an
expired card") so the person can tell the videos apart.

action start: begin filming the tab -> {recording, tab_id, name, started_at,
elapsed_ms, frames, note}. The person is asked unless the site is trusted. One
recording a tab, at most 3 at once.
action stop: end it and save it -> {tab_id, name, ended, file, bytes, duration_ms,
frames, upload}. Never asks. With no tab_id it stops the only recording, else the
active tab's. The video goes to Downloads/Wysebee Agent/; it is uploaded to the person's
Wysebee account only if they turned that on in the extension (off by default).
action status (the default): {recordings (those running), recent (the last saved,
each with its upload: uploading, uploaded, failed: ..., off, or not paired)}.

A recording also ends by itself after 15 minutes in all, 5 minutes after your last
action on the tab, or when the tab closes, the agent is paused or the debugging
bar is cancelled; what was filmed until then is still saved.

name.description: start: what the scenario is, at most 120 characters ("scenario" if omitted); it names the video.

tab_id.description: The tab; the active tab if omitted (stop: the only recording, if just one).

tools.name: browser_console
tools.description:
Read a tab's console: console.log/warn/error output, uncaught exceptions, and
the browser's own messages (failed loads, CSP violations, deprecations).

The first developer-tool call on a tab starts recording it, so messages logged
earlier may be missing — call browser_reload to capture a page from its start.
Recording carries on across navigations in that tab until it has been idle for
ten minutes. Chrome shows a "debugging this browser" bar on the tab meanwhile.

level.description:
The least severe level to include: "error" is errors only, "warning"
is warnings and errors, "all" is everything.

limit.description: How many of the newest entries to return, at most 1000.

after.description:
Only entries with a ``seq`` greater than this — pass the last seq you
saw to read just what is new.

clear.description: Empty the log after reading it.

tab_id.description: The tab; the active tab if omitted.

tools.name: browser_network
tools.description:
Read a tab's network log, as in the DevTools Network panel.

Recording starts with the first developer-tool call on a tab (see
browser_console); call browser_reload to capture every request a page makes as
it loads. Sign-in headers (Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, API keys) and
password-like fields in request bodies are always hidden.

filter.description: Only requests whose URL contains this text (case-insensitive).

resource_type.description:
Only this type: Document, Stylesheet, Image, Media, Font,
Script, XHR, Fetch, WebSocket, Manifest, Other.

failed_only.description: Only requests that failed or answered with status 400 or above.

include_headers.description: Add request and response headers and the request body.

limit.description: How many of the newest to return, at most 1000.

clear.description: Empty the log after reading it.

tab_id.description: The tab; the active tab if omitted.

tools.name: browser_network_body
tools.description:
Read the response body of one request from browser_network.

Text (HTML, JSON, JavaScript, CSS, XML) is returned, up to 100,000 characters;
for an image or other binary response only its type and size are. A body can
no longer be available once the page has moved far on.

tab_id.description: The tab it was made in; the active tab if omitted.

tools.name: browser_evaluate
tools.description:
Run JavaScript in the page and return its result, as in the DevTools console.

For anything the other tools do not cover: reading application state, the DOM,
localStorage, computed values, calling the page's own functions. Top-level
``await`` works. The result must be JSON-serialisable — return
``el.outerHTML`` or a plain object rather than a DOM element. Unless the site
is trusted the user is asked first, and sees the script. Times out after 15 s.

expression.description:
The JavaScript to run; the value of its last expression is the
result.

await_promise.description: Wait for a returned promise and give its value.

tab_id.description: The tab; the active tab if omitted.

tools.name: browser_viewport
tools.description:
Emulate a screen size — a phone, a tablet, a narrow window — or put it back.

The page is laid out at that size without resizing the user's window; take a
browser_screenshot to see it. The emulation lasts until ``reset`` or until the
tab's developer-tool session ends (ten minutes without a developer-tool call).

Common sizes: iPhone 15 390x844 at 3, Pixel 8 412x915 at 2.625, iPad 820x1180
at 2, laptop 1366x768, desktop 1920x1080.

width.description: Viewport width in CSS pixels, 200 to 5000.

height.description: Viewport height in CSS pixels, 200 to 5000.

device_scale_factor.description: Device pixel ratio, 0.5 to 4; 0 keeps the screen's own.

mobile.description: Emulate a mobile device: touch events and the mobile viewport.

user_agent.description: A user-agent string to send and report instead of the real one.

reset.description: Undo all of the above; the other arguments are ignored.

tab_id.description: The tab; the active tab if omitted.

tools.name: browser_inspect
tools.description:
Inspect one element, as in the DevTools Elements panel.

Returns its tag and attributes, its box (position, size, whether it is visible
and on screen), computed styles, accessible role and name, text and HTML.

ref.description: An element's ref from the latest browser_snapshot.

selector.description:
A CSS selector instead of ref; the result also says how many
elements match.

index.description: Which match of ``selector`` to inspect, from 0.

styles.description:
CSS properties to read (e.g. ["z-index", "overflow"]); a set that
decides layout and look if omitted.

tab_id.description: The tab; the active tab if omitted.

tools.name: browser_audit
tools.description:
Audit a page for common problems: accessibility (missing alt text, unlabeled
fields and buttons, low contrast, heading order, lang), SEO (title, meta
description, viewport, h1) and best practices (duplicate ids, mixed content,
oversized images, unsafe target=_blank).

A fast first pass, not Lighthouse. Each issue gives a count and a few example
elements; follow up with browser_inspect. Includes the console's error count
when the tab is being recorded.

tab_id.description: The tab; the active tab if omitted.

tools.name: browser_performance
tools.description:
Measure a page's performance.

Returns load timings (time to first byte, DOMContentLoaded, load), first and
largest contentful paint, cumulative layout shift, long tasks, resources by type
with the slowest five, DOM size, and Chrome's runtime counters (JS heap, nodes,
layouts, style recalculations, script time). Call browser_reload first for
numbers from a fresh load.

tab_id.description: The tab; the active tab if omitted.

tools.name: browser_reload
tools.description: Reload a tab, recording its console and network from the very start.

bypass_cache.description: Reload without the cache, like Shift+Reload.

tab_id.description: The tab; the active tab if omitted.

tools.name: browser_mock
tools.description:
Fake network responses on a tab, for testing how the app being developed handles
errors: answer an API call with a 500, fail it with ConnectionRefused, or hold it
back to test a slow server — then drive the page and see what a person would see.

Each rule picks requests by URL glob (and optionally method, resource type and
how many times) and says what happens: `status` (+ `headers`, `body`), `error`, or
`delay_ms` alone. The first matching rule with uses left wins; requests no rule
matches go on as normal. New rules are added after the tab's current ones; `clear`
drops those first, and `clear` with no `rules` stops faking. Called with no
arguments it lists the active rules. Returns {tab_id, origin, rules (each with its
hits), note}; faked requests show in browser_network.

Rules end when the tab goes to another site, the agent is paused, or after about
ten minutes without a developer-tool call. Whole pages are never faked, only what
a page loads. The person is asked each time unless the site is set to "Allow
everything".

url.description: The requests' full URL as a glob: * matches any run of characters, ? one character. Must start with http:, https: or *, such as */api/orders*.

method.description: Only requests with this method; any method if omitted.

resource_type.description: Only requests of this type; any if omitted. Never Document: whole pages are not faked.

times.description: Use the rule this many times, then let requests through; forever if omitted.

delay_ms.description: Wait this long first, 0 to 30000. Alone (no status or error) it holds the real request back, to test a slow server.

status.description: Answer with a fake response of this status, such as 500. Not with error.

headers.description: The fake response's headers. Set-Cookie, Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials are refused.

body.description: The fake response's body, at most 1,000,000 characters: a string, or any JSON value, sent as application/json.

error.description: Fail the request as the network would, such as ConnectionRefused. Not with status.

rules.description: Rules to add, at most 50 a tab. Checked whole: if one is wrong, none is added.

clear.description: Drop the tab's existing rules first; with no rules, just stop faking.

tab_id.description: The tab; the active tab if omitted.
